comment: D-PLY-35 (2026-10-28): the player slot's watchdog, derived from the helper's own bounds. Run by BOTH
tests/Model.test.js and tests/test_player_bounds.py. A number implemented in two languages gets one
fixture (engineering rule, dev branch).
`helper` is every bound a `player start|restart|probe` can wait out, in milliseconds, and `names` is
the helper's own name for each with its unit (bin/helper/01-core.py, 07-player.py): the python side
reads each off the helper by that name, so a bound that moves there without moving here is red. The
model mirrors the same numbers (Model.PLAYER_BOUNDS, and Model.STOP_QUIT_GRACE_MS and
STOP_KILL_GRACE_MS, which the stop ladder already shares); node compares them with `helper`.
`watchdogMs` is Model.playerWatchdogMs per verb, the shell's playerWatchdog interval while that verb
runs, and "" is the bound on the birth edge when no verb runs (unchanged from 12 s). The arithmetic,
with i = ipcMs, the longest path through the helper's code with every wait it survives at its full
bound plus the one wait that ends it (model/player.mjs says why each term is there):
ladder("")     = max(quitGraceMs, 2i) + killGraceMs + 2 settleMs        = 4000 + 2000 + 1000 = 7000
ladder("term") = killGraceMs + 2 settleMs                               = 3000
spawn          = settleConnectMs + spawnPidMs + 2 spawnMs + 2i          = 200 + 2000 + 10000 + 4000 = 16200
tail           = max(ladder("term") + settleConnectMs, i + firstLoadMs) = max(3200, 5000) = 5000
start   = lookupMs + lockMs + lockPollMs + 2i + carry + ladder("") + spawn + tail + relay + marginMs
(carry = 2i, restart on adoption, 2026-11-01: a found player ANOTHER build launched answers its probe and is
replaced, not adopted -- its volume, mute, fullscreen and pause read inside one ipcMs, the three set on the new
player inside another; walked at 42.07 s against the 38.25 s 43250 left, lane RA's M9.)
restart = lookupMs + lockMs + lockPollMs + ladder("term") + settleConnectMs + 2i + ladder("") + spawn + tail + relay + marginMs
(relay = relayStartMs + 3 relayIpcMs = 5000 + 3000, D-SINK-102, 2026-11-14: a spawn waits for its new relay's status;
a start or a restart asks a relay the adopted player's status, the load's registration and the first-load count.)
(lookupMs, D-SINK-101, 2026-11-13: player_target looks a cached channel's host name up before the lock; a
lookup answered just inside its bound is survived, one that reaches it refuses the channel, so a start and a
restart each sum it once; the walk spends it at the bound the code hands resolve_within.)
(a restart's own ladder can leave a player in uninterruptible sleep, and adopt_or_spawn then meets it as a
start does: probed and laddered from quit. Corrected by the recheck from 35450, which left that path out.)
probe   = max(3i, settleLockMs + lockPollMs + settleConnectMs) + relayIpcMs + marginMs = max(6000, 750) + 1000 + 5000 = 12000
play    = 8000 + relayIpcMs = 9000: the control slot's watchdog over one `play`, its fixed 8 s plus one relay question
(relayStaggerMs is in no sum: the relay starts its next connect attempt that long after one that has not answered,
inside the player's own load, which no verb waits on; a dead first answer costs a channel that much, not RELAY_CONNECT_S.)
tests/test_player_bounds.py also WALKS the shipping verbs' worst paths under a virtual clock and holds each
inside its `watchdogMs` less `marginMs`, so the composition is checked against the code and not only the leaves.
`boardMs` is the sum the board row named (lock + spawn + first load), which the old 12 s was under;
`previousMs` is that 12 s.
